title: How Claude Code Works - Jared Zoneraich, PromptLayer
talk_summary: Jared Zoneraich reverse-engineers Claude Code and other coding agents, arguing the winning architecture is a simple master while-loop over a few rigorous tool calls (bash, read, grep, edit-via-diff, task subagents) with heavy reliance on model flexibility and context management rather than DAGs, RAG, or classifiers. He also covers subagents for context isolation, todo lists as prompt-only planning, skills as lazy-loaded system-prompt extensions, and eval strategies (end-to-end, point-in-time, backtests, 'agent smell').

takeaways.technique: Subagents with isolated context returning only results
takeaways.what_they_do: Spawn a task/subagent with its own context window that does the noisy work (research, doc reading, test running, code review) and feeds back only a compact result to the main loop, keeping the master context short.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the key with the sub aent is it has its own context and it feeds back only the results and this is how you don't clutter it

takeaways.technique: Few rigorous tools, bash as universal adapter, diff-based edits
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the tool surface small (read/grep/edit/bash/task) and make edits as unified diffs rather than full-file rewrites; let bash cover the long tail instead of building dozens of bespoke tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's using diffs and it's not rewriting files most of the time. uh way faster, way way uh less context used

takeaways.technique: Prompt-only todo list for steerability and crash resume
takeaways.what_they_do: Inject a structured todo list (ids, titles, statuses) into the system prompt and instruct one-task-at-a-time completion; not enforced in code, purely instruction-following, giving resumability and progress visibility.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's not enforced deterministically. It's purely prompt based. It's purely in the system prompt.

takeaways.technique: Backtests and 'agent smell' metrics instead of benchmarks
takeaways.what_they_do: Capture historical inputs, rerun the agent over them, and track surface metrics like tool-call count, retry count, and latency as a sanity check; also run headless end-to-end tests through the agent SDK.
takeaways.evidence_quote: run an agent and see how many times does it call a tool call. How many times does it retry? How long does it take?

takeaways.what_they_do: Move long, task-specific instructions out of the always-loaded constitution into named skills with one-line descriptions the model invokes on demand, keeping baseline context small.
takeaways.evidence_quote: let's think of it as a extendable system prompt... we don't want to clutter the context

takeaways.technique: Handoff instead of compaction for long threads
takeaways.what_they_do: When context fills, start a fresh thread seeded with a curated handoff summary rather than paying for slow in-place compaction of the whole window.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's faster than reloading. And uh that's what handoff is. You're you're just starting a new thread
